title: Water and Earth Materials
seo_title: Water and Weathering Worksheets: Frost Wedging, Porosity and Stream Sediment (Earth Science)
standard_text: Plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and its effects on Earth materials and surface processes.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on water and Earth materials (NGSS HS-ESS2-5): water's properties, frost wedging, chemical weathering, porosity, permeability and stream sediment. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Freezing, dissolving and flowing water weather, move and deposit Earth materials.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water's special properties shape Earth's surface.

  • Expands 9% when frozen → frost wedging. Slightly acidic and polar → dissolves minerals, forms caves.
  • High heat capacity moderates climate; cohesion moves water through soil.
  • Faster streams carry bigger sediment; slowing water deposits it. Porosity = pore volume ÷ total × 100.
Example

200 mL of water freezes. Ice volume?

200 × 1.09

Answer: 218 mL

Example

400 mL sediment holds 120 mL water. Porosity?

120 ÷ 400

Answer: 30%

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water shrinks when it freezes.
  • Thinking clay drains water fastest.
  • Thinking slow streams can carry boulders.

faq.a: Water seeps into cracks, freezes and expands about 9%, prying the rock apart (frost wedging). Slightly acidic water also dissolves some minerals.

faq.q: What is the difference between porosity and permeability?
faq.a: Porosity is how much open space a material has. Permeability is how easily water flows through it, which needs connected spaces.
When a river slows down, it no longer has enough energy to carry larger particles, so they settle out.

items.q: How do limestone caves form?

items.q: What is frost wedging?
